subject: Storage lifecycle & data sanitization Q&A for PHI-bearing workloads

Subject: Storage lifecycle questions for PHI workloads

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — MedInsight is excited about the latency and cost numbers. Before we move further, our security and compliance teams need clarity on two scenarios we commonly run into:

1) Short-lived retention for user-identifiable content (30–90 days) but long-lived non-identifiable logs (1+ year). Can Redwood support per-tenant retention floors and automatic scrub that removes PII/PHI fields while keeping analytic signals?

2) When a user exercises a deletion/ERASURE request, can you perform a full purge (including model cache/KV) within 24–72 hours, and do you produce evidence/audit logs we can import into our governance portal?

Attached is our initial audit checklist. High-level answers will suffice now — procurement is waiting on a short summary to proceed with PoC scoping.

Subject: Re: Storage lifecycle questions for PHI workloads

Hi Jill — great questions and thanks for sharing the checklist. Below is a concise breakdown of options and what we typically implement for regulated customers. I also attached a short implementation proposal for the PoC.

High-level approach:
- Tenant-scoped retention policies: Yes — you can set per-tenant retention windows for raw inputs, outputs, and derived logs independently. Policies are enforced at the ingestion layer and by scheduled retention jobs.
- Field-level sanitization vs irreversible deletion:
  - For analytics retention, we recommend field-level pseudonymization (HMAC or reversible tokenization with customer-managed keys) for 30–90 day windows so analytic signals remain usable.
  - For legal erasure requests, we support both irreversible scrub (cryptographic shredding of stored blobs and metadata) and an option to soft-delete then scrub after a short verification window.
- Model cache (KV) and ephemeral state: KV caches are tenant-scoped and can be invalidated on-demand. For erasure requests we can evict relevant keys within the 24–72 hour target; for stronger guarantees we run a targeted KV sweep during the next maintenance window (we can commit to the timeline in the PoC).
- Auditability and evidence: We emit immutable audit events for retention-policy changes, delete requests, cache evictions, and scrub operations. Events are queryable via an export endpoint (JSON) and we can push a digest to your governance S3 or a secure Drive link.

Tradeoffs and recommended defaults for PHI:
- 30-day full retention + 1 year analytics (pseudonymized) is a common pattern that balances risk and product telemetry value.
- If your legal requirements demand irreversible deletion on request, expect reduced ability to re-run past analysis that relies on identifiers. We can provide synthetic/aggregated backups instead.

Attachments: data-lifecycle-proposal.xlsx (stub) — contains sample configs, ML-impact notes, and PoC milestones.

Hi Jill / procurement — quick one-page summary below to unblock you for PoC scope.

One-page summary (answers to procurement):
1) Artifacts: Attached — SOC2-snapshot.pdf and redaction-playbook.md (playbook describes field-level scrub rules, HMAC tokenization, and irreversible shredding process). We also provided the PoC config workbook.
2) Timelines: For the PoC we can commit to a 48-hour guaranteed window for full tenant-scoped KV eviction + scrub of stored blobs. Operational note: we can hit 24 hours for small tenant footprints (low KV volume) but must provision the 48-hour SLA for larger datasets until we validate performance during the PoC.
3) Cost delta: No platform feature flag or license delta for enabling hard-delete in the PoC. For production at scale, very large-volume guaranteed scrub (24-hour SLA at petabyte scale) may incur an engineering ops premium; we will surface estimates in the SOW if you choose that guarantee.
